title: Readiness and process launch are separate operations
summary: Deployment may prepare and optionally launch a declared process, but process start is not automatically part of repair/readiness. Existing-process detection must distinguish absent, expected, different, stale and unknown rather than accepting a similar command line.
invariants: Repair/readiness can complete while application workers remain stopped.
Starting a worker/service requires an explicit process requirement or application action.
A similar command string is not sufficient identity for RUNNING_EXPECTED.
Launch environment is explicit and should not depend blindly on interactive shell startup files.
Deployment owns launch mechanics, not what the application subsequently computes.

provenance.claim: Defines explicit launch environment and ProcessRequirement.
Defines existing process states and rejects command-string-only identity.
Audio readiness remains separate from worker start.
